# Maxence Poutord

> Personal website of Maxence Poutord, a software engineer with more than 10 years working in the industry.

Maxence Poutord is a software engineer and public speaker. This site holds his blog (web development, engineering culture, career), a few free web apps, and a personal recipe collection. Content is written in English unless noted otherwise.

## Blog posts

- [How Computers Learned to Talk Like Humans](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/how-computers-learned-to-talk-like-humans/): From the Turing Test to ChatGPT — how computers went from scripted chatbots like ELIZA to Markov chains, word embeddings, and Transformers, and how "guess the next word" became conversation.
- [Lessons learned from building my first 3D Video Game](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/lessons-learned-from-building-my-first-3d-video-game/): Key lessons from building Avion, a 3D flight simulator — covering performance optimisation (frustum culling, LOD, hardware instancing), physics (gimbal lock, quaternions), and the tradeoffs between realism and fun.
- [Anatomy of a Crypto Scam - Thomas Harris](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/crypto-scam-with-ai/): I investigated Thomas Harris, an AI-generated YouTuber who uses fake crypto tutorials to scam people.
- [10 Years of Blogging, what I learned](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/10-years-of-blogging/): Reflects on my experience and sharing some key lessons learned after 10y of blogging. Including the importance of writing a good title, not worrying about post popularity...
- [How to integrate Giscus to your Astro Blog](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/giscus-with-astro/): Learn how to integrate Giscus (GitHub-powered comments), into your Astro blog. How to deal with dark mode and styles customization.
- [A Look Inside My Personalized .gitconfig](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/gitconfig/): Boost your Git efficiency! A simple config for a smoother workflow.
- [From Gatsby.js to Astro](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/hello-astro/): How I migrated my website from Gatsby.js to Astro. What I liked about Astro and some problems I encountered during the migration.
- [Using Notion as a CMS for Gatsby.js](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/notion-as-cms-gatsby/): How I use Notion as a CMS for my website built with Gatsby.js. The script can also be used with different static site generator like Astro and Next.js
- [Improving Core Web Vitals of a React Application](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/improving-core-web-vitals-react-app/): A case study of changes implemented to improve the performances of a React application.
- [How to publish an npm package for ESM and CommonJS with TypeScript](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/publish-npm-package-esm-and-cjs/): A step by step tutorial on how to publish an npm package for ECMAScript Modules (ESM) and CommonJS (CJS) with TypeScript
- [How to play Age of Empire II DE on MacOS](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/aoe2-on-macos/): The complete guide on how to play Age of Empire 2 when you have a Mac (CrossOver or GeForce NOW). Also includes my personal hotkeys and mods.
- [Turborepo: a Monorepo Revolution](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/turborepo/): My thoughts about Turborepo, a tool that facilitates your monorepo management.
- [Simpler context switching with Git worktrees](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/git-worktrees/): git worktree allows you to attach a branch to a specific folder. It's like doing a clone of a repository that shares the same git folder.
- [2021 - A Year In Review](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/2021-a-year-in-review/): A look back at 2021: joining Orderfox as a Senior Software Engineer, 5 blog posts, side projects, travel, and the goals I set for 2022.
- [My Journey with RSI (as a Software Engineer)](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/rsi-as-developer/): Some strategies I implemented to overcoming Repetitive Strain Injury (RSI)
- [Vue.js: Let's Scale!](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/vue-js-module-architecture/): Architecture and technical decision behind a big Vue.js application.
- [Lessons Learned by Maintaining a Large Codebase](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/lesson-learned-maintaining-large-vue-js-codebase/): I've been maintaining a massive Vue.js codebase for the last 3 years. Here are 9 lessons I've learned along the way.
- [Bash for developers](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/bash-for-dev/): Essential bash commands and time-saving aliases to simplify your daily tasks
- [2020 - A Year In Review](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/2020-a-year-in-review/): A look back at 2020: frontend infrastructure, accessibility (WCAG AA), testing, side projects, and the goals I set for 2021.
- [Monorepo: is it worth jumping the bandwagon?](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/monorepo-pros-and-cons/): Monorepos: beyond the hype. when and when not) to use them.
- [Tips for your GitHub Portfolio](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/tips-for-your-github-portfolio/): Showcasing your work can help you land your dream job. But you have to follow a few simple rules.
- [Vue.js Performance Improvement with Memoization](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/vuejs-performance-improvement-with-memoization/): How I reduced the rendering of a complex component by 10 (from ~4s to ~0.3s).
- [Vue.js Testing Made Easy (with Testing Library)](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/vue-js-testing-library/): How Testing Library helps you to write better integration test
- [How to mock Axios HTTP calls with Jest](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/jest-mock-axios-calls/): How to unit test components that have HTTP calls.
- [async/await without try...catch!](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/async-await-without-try-catch/): A cool wrapper to write promises without using a try...catch block
- [Why you shouldn't pay too much attention to your code coverage](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/code-coverage/): High code coverage doesn't guarantee quality: You can write tests that cover every line but miss edge cases or core functionality.
- [10 Tips for Working From Home](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/10-tips-for-working-from-home/): Since the pandemic, most developers have been forced to work from home. I've been working remotely for over 2 years now. Here are some tips to make this period a little bit less painful.
- [10 Tips for Writing Better Tests](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/10-tips-write-better-tests/): 1. Think documentation 2. Isolate your tests 3. Keep it flat 4.Only mock what you can't control 5. Avoid assertion in loops (forEach/...) 6...
- [How to generate social share images with Gatsby](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/generate-social-image-share-with-gatsby/): How I created dynamic Open Graph images for my Gatsby website
- [2019 - A Year In Review](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/2019-a-year-in-review/): A look back at 2019: scaling a large Vue.js application, frontend infrastructure, remote work from Asia, and the goals I set for 2020.
- [Git: Cheat Sheet (advanced)](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/git-cheat-sheet/): A Git Cheat Sheet that focuses on Essential Commands for Experienced Developers.
- [How to mock Date with Jest](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/jest-mock-date/): A guide on how to deal with unit tests that uses the JavaScript Date object.
- [What's happens when you "git commit"](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/git-under-the-hood/): Understanding the Git Folder Structure and how git works under the hood.
- [Digital Nomad: the Golden Ticket?](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/busting-nomad-myths/): Don't trust the influencers. Working from the beach doesn't work.
- [Two months in Canggu as a Digital Nomad](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/nomad-in-canggu/): My global review and my budget breakdown after living and working remotely in Bali for 60 days
- [Enhance your git log with conventional commits](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/git-conventional-commits/): Standards to write more explicit commits messages.
- [2018 - A Year In Review](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/2018-a-year-in-review/): A look back at 2018: leaving HostelWorld for VSware, going 100% remote, starting a nomadic life, and the goals I set for 2019.
- [3 Tips for Scaling Large Vue.js Application](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/3-tips-scaling-vue-application/): 1. Split your application into completely isolated modules. 2. Consider micro-frontends architecture. 3. Don't put everything in the Vuex Store
- [My first month in Lisbon as a Digital Nomad](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/nomad-in-lisbon/): My first month in Lisbon as a digital nomad: accommodation, meeting people, the best places to work from, useful mobile apps, and my overall feedback.
- [Hello GatsbyJS!](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/hello-gatsby/): Why I migrated my blog from Jekyll to GatsbyJS after 3 years: what I liked about Jekyll, what pushed me away, and what Gatsby brings.
- [Immutability in JavaScript (without library)](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/immutability-js-without-library/): A deep dive into JS immutability, guiding you on how to achieve it without relying on external libraries.
- [Typical JavaScript interview exercises (explained)](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/js-exercises-explained/): Level up your JavaScript interview skills! This post tackles common exercises, offering clear explanations to help you ace the coding challenge.
- [A la découverte d'Hubot](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/hubot/): Découverte d'Hubot, le bot de GitHub : à quoi il sert, comment l'installer et écrire ses propres scripts pour automatiser son équipe via le chat.
- [Mon expat à Dublin](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/expatriation-en-irlande/): Huit mois après avoir quitté Nantes pour Dublin : pourquoi partir, le logement, le travail, le coût de la vie, et est-ce que ça vaut le coup.
- [Chaining Javascript filters recursively](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/chaining-filter-js/): How to apply an unknown number of filters to a JavaScript collection, with a recursive filter function instead of an imperative loop — and why extending Array.prototype is a bad idea.
- [No more for/while loop in JavaScript](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/no-more-loop-in-js/): Some alternatives to traditional for/while loops in JavaScript. Also how to address set theory with array of objects (union, intersection and difference).
- [Github: Tips&tricks](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/github-tips-and-tricks/): Level up your GitHub game with these tips & tricks.
- [2016 - A Year In Review](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/2016-a-year-in-review/): A look back at 2016: switching to Linux, moving from Nantes to Dublin, speaking at conferences, and the SMART goals I set for 2017.
- [PHP et Programmation fonctionnelle](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/programmation-fonctionnelle-php/): Les concepts clefs de la programmation fonctionnelle appliqués à PHP : immuabilité, récursion, fonctions d'ordre supérieur, fonctions pures et mémoïsation.
- ["Else": the unnecessary expression](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/else-unnecessary-expression/): How to write code without the traditional "else"
- [Dealing with Enum in a Symfony App with Doctrine2 as ORM](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/dealing-with-enum-symfony-doctrine/): How to handle Enums in a Symfony application with Doctrine2, with a reusable abstract PHP Enum class, entity validation and a Symfony choice form type — no database-specific ENUM column.
- [Vagrant, Symfony and Windows are not incompatibles](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/vagrant-symfony-windows/): Tips to speed up a Symfony application running in a Vagrant box on Windows: NFS shared folders, the vbguest and winnfsd plugins, and cache tuning.
- [La qualité logicielle et les trois petits cochons](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/qualite-logicielle-3-petits-cochons/): Un comparatif entre le conte pour enfants et la qualité logicielle
- [Une stack Docker pour votre application Symfony](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/docker-pour-symfony/): Une stack Docker complète pour développer une application Symfony : nginx, PHP-FPM, MySQL, Redis, la stack ELK et PHPMyAdmin avec docker-compose.
- [Utiliser Redis pour stocker le cache de Doctrine](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/cache-doctrine-avec-redis/): Améliorer les performances de doctrine en utilisant son cache et en stockant les informations sur Redis
- [Productivité Ninja !](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/productivite-ninja/): Retour d'expérience sur la mise en oeuvre de certaines pratiques telles que les TODO list, pomodoro...
- [A la découverte d'APISpark](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/a-la-decouverte-d-apispark/): Retour d'expérience avec la plateforme APISpark
- [REST, CRUD et bonnes pratiques](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/rest-crud/): Guide de bonnes pratiques pour les API REST CRUD
- [Atom, un éditeur qui vous veut du bien](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/atom/): Retour d'expérience avec l'éditeur de texte Atom
- [Utilisez un framework PHP](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/utilisez-un-framework-php/): Pourquoi utiliser un framework PHP open source plutôt qu'un framework maison : capitalisation, vélocité, performances — et les cas où il vaut mieux s'en passer.
- [Non, votre API n'est pas REST !](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/rest-rmm-model/): Le modèle de maturité de Richardson (RMM) explique pourquoi la plupart des API dites REST n'atteignent jamais le niveau 3 (HATEOAS).
- [Hadopi : fonctionnement et contournement](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/hadopi/): Comment fonctionne la surveillance HADOPI du P2P, et quelles alternatives (seedbox, VPN, newsgroups) existent pour ne plus être concerné.
- [vagrant up et dites adieu à WAMP !](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/vagrant/): Présentation et installation de Vagrant
- [Mémo - Commandes Symfony2](https://www.maxpou.fr/blog/commandes-sf2/): Liste des commandes console utilisées lors du développement d’un projet sous Symfony2
